text: If I'd known about the storm, I wouldn't have set sail.
tip: 'wouldn't have' sounds like /ˈwʊdntəv/. Stress KNOWN, STORM and SAIL.

text: The lake is said to have been home to a dragon for centuries.
tip: Chunk it: The lake is said | to have been home to a dragon | for centuries. 'centuries' is /ˈsentʃəriz/.

text: Not only did she win the race, but she also broke the record.
tip: Stress ON-ly, WIN, AL-so and REC-ord (the noun has stress on the first syllable).

text: By this time next year, I'll have finished my degree.
tip: 'I'll have' squeezes into /aɪl əv/. 'finished' ends in /t/: /ˈfɪnɪʃt/.

text: She's been working on the project for months, so she must be exhausted.
tip: 'exhausted' is /ɪɡˈzɔːstɪd/: the h is silent and the stress is on the second syllable.

text: Despite the heavy rain, thousands of people turned up for the concert.
tip: 'thousands' /ˈθaʊzndz/ starts with tongue between teeth. 'turned up' links into 'tur-nup'.

text: I'd rather you didn't mention it to anyone else.
tip: 'mention it' links into 'men-shun-it', and 'anyone else' flows together: /ˈeniwʌn els/.

text: The knight, whose armour was dented, refused to give up.
tip: 'knight' has a silent k: /naɪt/. 'armour' is /ˈɑːmə/ in British English. 'dented' ends in /ɪd/.

text: It's high time we did something about the pollution in the river.
tip: Stress HIGH TIME, SOME-thing, pol-LU-tion and RIV-er.

text: You can't have seen her at the market; she was with me all morning.
tip: 'can't have' is /kɑːnt əv/. Make a short pause at the semicolon.

text: Having finished her homework, Mia went outside to play with the fox.
tip: Pause after 'homework'. 'finished' ends in /t/, not /ɪd/.

text: The more you practise, the more confident you'll become.
tip: Give both halves the same beat: the MORE you PRAC-tise | the MORE CON-fident you'll be-COME.

text: Hardly anyone noticed that the crown had been stolen.
tip: 'crown' rhymes with 'brown' /aʊ/. 'stolen' and 'noticed' have /əʊ/.

text: I'm considering whether to accept the job or carry on studying.
tip: 'carry on' links with a little y sound: 'carry-yon'. Stress con-SID-er-ing and ac-CEPT.

text: The bakery was so crowded that we had to wait outside for ages.
tip: 'crowded' has an extra syllable /ˈkraʊdɪd/. 'had to' is /ˈhæd tə/ with one t.

text: Whatever happens, make sure you keep the map somewhere safe.
tip: 'sure' is /ʃɔː/ in British English and 'safe' is /seɪf/. Don't mix up /ʃ/ and /s/.

text: He apologised for being late, claiming that his horse had lost a shoe.
tip: a-POL-o-gised ends in /d/: /əˈpɒlədʒaɪzd/. 'horse' has /ɔː/ and no 'r' sound.

q: What would you have done differently last year? Use 'I would have' or 'I wish I had'.
keywords: would have|wish i had|wish i would
model: Looking back, I would have spent less time online and more time outdoors.
tip: 'would have' is often /ˈwʊdəv/, and 'I'd have' is fine too. Stress the things you'd change.

q: Should people work from home? Give both sides with 'On the one hand' and 'on the other hand'.
model: On the one hand, working from home saves time, but on the other hand, people can feel lonely.
tip: Pause after each signpost phrase and stress ONE and OTH-er.

q: Describe a place you would like to visit. Use 'I've always wanted to'.
model: I've always wanted to visit Iceland because I'd love to see the northern lights.
tip: 'wanted to' is /ˈwɒntɪd tə/ with a weak 'to'. Stress AL-ways and the place name.

q: Tell me about a problem in your town. Use a passive like 'needs to be' or 'should be' + past participle.
keywords: needs to be|need to be|should be|must be|ought to be|has to be|have to be
model: The old bridge needs to be repaired because it's getting dangerous.
tip: Keep 'to be' weak /tə bi/ and stress the participle: re-PAIRED.

q: Compare life in a city and life in a village. Use 'whereas' or 'while'.
model: City life is exciting and fast, whereas village life is quieter and more relaxed.
tip: 'whereas' is /weərˈæz/ with stress on the second syllable. Pause just before it.

text: If we'd left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the start of the match.
tip: 'we'd' is one beat /wiːd/ and 'wouldn't have' is /ˈwʊdntəv/. Stress LEFT, EAR-li-er and MATCH.

text: The new science lab is being built next to the sports hall.
tip: 'being' has two syllables /ˈbiːɪŋ/ and 'built' rhymes with 'kilt'. Stress SCI-ence LAB and BUILT.

text: Our team, which hadn't won all season, finally lifted the trophy.
tip: Pause at both commas and drop your voice a little for 'which hadn't won all season'. TRO-phy is /ˈtrəʊfi/.

text: I wish I'd brought my camera to the dolphin show.
tip: 'I'd brought' is /aɪd brɔːt/: the 'gh' is silent. Stress WISH and DOL-phin.

text: By the time we reached the summit, the clouds had completely cleared.
tip: Pause after 'summit'. 'clouds' and 'cleared' start with the same /kl/. Stress com-PLETE-ly.

text: She's used to getting up early for swimming training.
tip: 'used to' here is /juːst tə/, with an /s/ not a /z/. Stress EAR-ly and SWIM-ming.

text: The rescued turtles will be released back into the ocean next week.
tip: 'rescued' is two syllables /ˈreskjuːd/. 'ocean' is /ˈəʊʃn/ with a /ʃ/ in the middle.

text: You'd better wear a helmet if you're going skateboarding.
tip: 'You'd better' is /juːd ˈbetə/: the 'd' is tiny but there. Stress HEL-met and SKATE-board-ing.

text: Unless we recycle more, the school bins will keep overflowing.
tip: re-CY-cle is stressed in the middle /riːˈsaɪkl/. Stress o-ver-FLOW-ing near the end.

text: Volunteers are needed to help clean up the beach on Saturday.
tip: vol-un-TEERS is stressed on the last part. Link 'clean up' into 'clea-nup'.

q: What's the best way to stay healthy? Use 'It's important to'.
model: It's important to get enough sleep and to play sport a few times a week.
tip: 'It's important to' is quick: /ɪts ɪmˈpɔːtnt tə/. Stress SLEEP and SPORT.

q: Describe a time you felt proud of yourself. Use 'I managed to'.
model: Last term I managed to finish a five-kilometre fun run without stopping once.
tip: 'managed' is /ˈmænɪdʒd/, two syllables. Stress FIN-ish and STOP-ping.

q: Would you rather explore space or the deep ocean? Use 'I'd rather' and 'because'.
model: I'd rather explore the deep ocean because there are still creatures nobody has ever seen.
tip: 'I'd rather' is /aɪd ˈrɑːðə/. Pause a little before 'because', then stress the reason.

q: Tell me about a club you'd like to join. Use 'I'm interested in'.
model: I'm interested in joining the robotics club because I love building things that move.
tip: IN-ter-est-ed has three or four beats, stressed at the start. After 'in', use -ing: 'interested in JOIN-ing'.

q: How has your town or school changed? Use the present perfect, like 'has been built' or 'have opened'.
keywords: has been|have been|has opened|have opened|has changed|have changed|has become|have become
model: A new skate park has been built, and two bakeries have opened on the high street.
tip: 'has been' is weak /həz bɪn/. Stress the new things: SKATE PARK and BA-ke-ries.

q: Should mobile phones be allowed at school? Give your view with 'Personally' and a reason.
model: Personally, I think phones should stay in our bags, because they distract us in lessons.
tip: Pause after 'Personally,'. PER-son-al-ly is stressed on the first syllable.

q: Explain how to look after a pet fish. Use 'make sure'.
model: Make sure you feed it only a little every day and clean the tank every two weeks.
tip: 'sure' is /ʃɔː/ in British English. Stress LIT-tle, CLEAN and TANK.

q: What would happen if it snowed all week? Start with 'If it snowed'.
model: If it snowed all week, the school would probably close and we could build a giant snowman.
tip: Pause after 'all week,'. 'would' is weak /wəd/. Stress PROB-ab-ly and GI-ant SNOW-man.
